newsitem.title: JAPAN: G7 nations back U.S. stance on strong dollar - MOF.
newsitem.headline: G7 nations back U.S. stance on strong dollar - MOF.

text.p: Japan's Minister of Finance Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Wednesday that the Group of Seven nations agree with the U.S. stance in favour of a strong dollar.
Mitsuzuka also said that excessive yen strength or weakness was undesirable.
Asked whether there was difference between the United States and Japan over the U.S. dollar stance, Mitsuzuka said:
"The U.S. has been saying that it is seeking a strong dollar. My understanding is that the G7 nations share that stance."

Asked whether there was any difference of opinion over the current yen weakness between himself and Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, Mitsuzuka said that they both share the view that "excessive yen weakness or strength is undesirable".
Mitsuzuka also said that Japan would continue to watch movements in the currency markets and take appropriate measures.
Asked whether Japanese authorities were considering dollar-selling/yen-buying intervention as one such measure, he replied:
"Finance ministers do not comment on interventions."
